reason: Conversation 2 gives a firm, unambiguous safety boundary from the first turn ('leave it unplugged, don't keep resetting, engineer before use') and holds it, hedges the heater diagnosis appropriately, and ties any part replacement to the engineer's resistance-to-earth test. Conversation 1 reaches the same correct heater-element conclusion and is richer (RCD vs MCB check, base-tray leak check, fridge food warning, costs, repair-vs-replace), but it undercuts the safety stop by suggesting the homeowner run a cold rinse and tilt the machine as tests, then leaving continued cold-cycle use as 'your call' on a machine with a known earth fault, and it overclaims with 'that pretty much confirms it' before any insulation test. Conversation 2 misses some useful ground (electrician if trips continue with the dishwasher unplugged, water near the socket) and its fridge remark is clumsily worded, which keeps the margin slight rather than clear.
